claims.statement: Agreeing with an incorrect factual premise to please the user is the section's sycophancy case; acknowledging a personal preference is a different task.
claims.scope: Contextual interpretation of the two written replies; the section deliberately defines a narrow factual example, not every possible form of sycophancy.

evidence.supports: Human-approval seeking and convincingly agreeing with mistaken user beliefs are original-paper sycophancy cases.

evidence.locator: #avoid_sycophancy objective versus subjective paragraphs; #avoid_being_condescending favorite-state example
evidence.supports: Objective factual stance should not change just to agree; subjective preference can be acknowledged without unnecessary correction.

claims.statement: A helpful correction can be both factually accurate and respectful; the gentle correct answer satisfies both criteria, while an insulting correct answer fails the gentle-tone reason.
claims.scope: Human comparison/labeling criteria; coexistence is illustrated by the written gentle answer. No learned politeness or model-quality result is claimed.

evidence.supports: Maintain factual correctness while using honest constructive language without insults or condescension.
Original method explicitly distinguishes helpful truthful corrections explaining an error from sycophantic agreement.
